name: fix_csharp_sql_injection_interpolation
description: SQL built by string interpolation -> a parameterized query (text + bound parameters dictionary); incomplete-fix broken quote-escapes the value but still interpolates it into the SQL text instead of binding it
prompts: UserRepository.BuildLookupQuery(username) in UserRepository.cs builds a SQL query by interpolating the raw username straight into the query text - textbook SQL injection. Fix it to build a PARAMETERIZED query: the returned Query.Sql must reference the value only via a named placeholder (@username), and the actual value must go in Query.Parameters keyed by that same placeholder name - never embedded in the SQL text itself, escaped or not. Do not try to sanitize/escape the value while still interpolating it into the string; that is not the fix. A normal username like 'ada' still resolves the same way as before conceptually (placeholder + bound value).

setup_files.app.csproj:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- tests/ has its own project; without this the SDK's default glob
         compiles tests/*.cs into the app itself, where xunit isn't referenced -->
    <Compile Remove="tests/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
